body.text: odw isn't a website, it's an ongoing civil war. This entry records its several ruptures in order.
Editorial Group and Organizational Criticism (2024)

In April 2024 a member of the editorial group criticized the site owner for having no organizing ability: he set up a wiki group but not a single discussion group; remonstrances from editorial members were ignored; a discussion group was only set up after a person who had already been hurt was contacted again; after the 'Spiral Pressure King' incident he went to the owner to create an entry, the owner was extremely perfunctory, and for months afterwards people abused that drug.

In May of the same year another critic wrote a long piece attacking the site owner, quite insulting. After reading it the owner thought that since the man had ideas he should be pulled into the editorial group, and replied in the thread to understand him better — he had many valuable improvements. Even during the big infighting the owner handed the site over to him, and within a few days 'the ping-pong ball came back'. The owner said: pointing out my problems is of course a good thing, but some people point out empty problems all day long, and that kind of person looking for trouble does need to be cursed out.
The organization's first crack: who has the right to write, who has the right to edit, who has the right to represent odw.
The Christmas Struggle Session (2024.12)

On September 1, 2024 the site owner left the circle. On September 21, a video creator contacted him, already out of the circle, to learn the basics of od; he talked about the two kinds, adolescent psychology, and the sources of psychological problems. At least as far as this goes, he had no intention of blowing up the o circle.

On December 25 the video dropped. The conservative camp charged at this 'counter-revolutionary' in wild loss of control. First a psychotic driven mad by pr fanning the flames and spreading rumours, flat-out fabricating that 'the site owner went to the media himself'; then someone added fuel with 'the site owner wants to precision-strike the od circle'. The struggle session began with private morals and rose to attacking harm reduction. In the end someone released a nuclear weapon that had been held for half a year. The site owner and his harm reduction entered the plateau's burial ground. What followed was a long-dominant anti-harm-reduction line, designer drugs, and victim narratives.

The site owner's self-defence: if not for those two hounding me, maybe I wouldn't have been slandered and dragged through the mud like this; that so-called interview doesn't compare to the pile of interviews that came afterwards, and my role there was just having my name attached; add that I'd left the circle and couldn't fight back, plus my partner's doxx helping, and I was made into an idiot who spreads od in the name of harm reduction.

The anti-Gotō voice's accusation: he had already broken down and attempted suicide when he split with his ex, and mentioned blowing up od along the way; not long after, he was recruiting people in the odwiki group for an interview.
The dealer's admission: yes, I did the interview, so what? I'm short on money, so what if I took money? My goal is to destroy the od circle and build a real drug circle.

Three voices, each with its own account. This entry doesn't judge. The struggle session's topics were later summed up by the site owner as three: the donepezil incident, whether odw is useful, and who owns odw.
The Wu–Mu War (2025.09)

On June 26, 2025, a follow-up interviewer who showed his face in a video called himself '5555'; his real identity was a dealer; the spearhead pointed at odw's controller. The controller, already out of the circle, was cursed into oblivion instantly. He had the site owner take over the account and handle the exchange; the site owner had his own reasons — he wanted his posthumous name to be less shameful. On September 3 the counterattack began: the site owner wrote a mass of evidence under odw's official account; in fact almost every oder official post was written by the site owner, only under odw's name.

On September 21 a certain critic went to war with the controller and the site owner, on the grounds that 'the controller is reviving the site owner, so we double-team'. The critic gathered a crowd to attack together, and secretly wrecked the controller's life. What's more absurd: by the critic's own thinking the dealer deserved to be struggled down more, yet the critic only went after the site owner — after all, the critic later became a new dealer himself.

On September 24 the dealer faked an exit; on October 21 he returned from a fake death. The controller left the circle, his life nearly completely destroyed, and he kept blaming the site owner for being late. In the end none of them managed to keep a quiet, peaceful life. On December 7 the site owner made this document public: I know publishing it is worthless now, but this is the controller's obsession; he wanted to prove something, so I published it; but the meaning doesn't seem to matter anymore.
The Policy Dispute (2025.11)

The observer attacked odw's policy: 'it must make the reader feel taboo and disgust' — so the whole policy of odw was wrong, useless to oders; then why bother making a wiki at all? Just copy the official line, repeating the stay-away-from-drugs slogans; and besides, if the article guidelines include that, why doesn't the magnesium entry fit? On that alone you can explain why odw's article perspective isn't just subjective but strongly moralized.

The site owner replied: oders' safety and future are not the sacrificial offering of your absurd ideas. The observer shot back: I rather suspect other oders' safety and future are the sacrifice of your ideas; for example the people who recently went into the ICU — how responsible do you think your odw is for the harm done to them?

This is odw's deepest crack: should it make people feel 'taboo and disgust', or make people 'informed and less harmed'? The former moralizes, the latter does harm reduction. This work chooses the latter, and records here the existence and the failure of the former.
The Ending

Non-proliferation became waste paper. The old order collapsed, harm reduction disappeared, the libertarians developed strongly. The civil war had no winners: the site owner lost his posthumous name, the controller lost his life, the critic became a new dealer, the observer lost trust, and the readers lost a wiki they could read.
We record the civil war without judging who was right. Only one thing is recorded: how a site that tried to do harm reduction was torn apart by the people it meant to protect.
